# 1. Import data and codebook

This file contains the analysis workflow for Dissertation Aim 1.

The current code uses the synthetic dataset. Code developed here will be updated and rerun using the real registry data after the initial descriptive and quality-control review is complete.

```{r import-data}
# ============================================================
# FILE PATHS — UPDATE BEFORE RUNNING ON THE REAL DATA
# ============================================================

# ---- UPDATE PATH 1: DATASET ----
data_file <- "data/raw/synthetic_data.csv"

# ---- UPDATE PATH 2: MASTER CODEBOOK ----
codebook_file <- "Dissertation_Aim1_Master_Codebook.xlsx"


# ============================================================
# IMPORT DATA AND CODEBOOK — NO PATH CHANGES NEEDED BELOW HERE
# ============================================================

# Import dataset
dat <- read_csv(data_file)

# Import codebook sheets
region_codes  <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Region Codes")
comuna_codes  <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Comuna Codes")
closure_codes <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Closure Codes")
country_codes <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Country Codes")
```

# 2. Create date and calendar year variables

The variable `fecha_creacion_caso` contains the date of case creation as a character variable (for example, `10OCT2012`).

This section converts it to an R date and derives calendar year.

```{r create-date-year}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    fecha_creacion_date = parse_date(
      fecha_creacion_caso,
      format = "%d%b%Y",
      locale = locale("en")
    ),
    year = lubridate::year(fecha_creacion_date)
  )
```

# 3. Define preliminary analytic sample

The planned Aim 1 study population includes individuals ages 15–65 with case creation dates from 2005–2023.

For now, the analytic sample is restricted only by age and calendar year.

The appropriate FEP/NAPD case eligibility criterion based on IPD confirmation/discard status will be added after the IPD variables are clarified using the real registry data.

## Sample flow

The table below shows the number of observations remaining after applying the currently established eligibility criteria sequentially.

```{r sample-flow}
analytic_sample_flow <- tibble(
  Step = c(
    "Raw dataset",
    "Age 15-65 years",
    "Age 15-65 years and calendar year 2005-2023"
  ),
  N = c(
    nrow(dat),

    dat %>%
      filter(
        !is.na(edad_ano_creacion_caso),
        between(edad_ano_creacion_caso, 15, 65)
      ) %>%
      nrow(),

    dat %>%
      filter(
        !is.na(edad_ano_creacion_caso),
        between(edad_ano_creacion_caso, 15, 65),
        !is.na(year),
        between(year, 2005, 2023)
      ) %>%
      nrow()
  )
)

kable(analytic_sample_flow)
```

## Create preliminary analytic dataset

The original imported dataset (`dat`) is preserved.

A separate dataset called `analytic_dat` is created containing observations that meet the currently established age and calendar-year criteria.

```{r create-analytic-dataset}
analytic_dat <- dat %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(edad_ano_creacion_caso),
    between(edad_ano_creacion_caso, 15, 65),
    !is.na(year),
    between(year, 2005, 2023)
  )

# ============================================================
# TODO: ADD FINAL FEP/NAPD CASE ELIGIBILITY CRITERION HERE
#
# The appropriate use of ipd_cofirmado and/or ipd_descartado
# will be determined after reviewing the real registry data.
# ============================================================
```

## Verify sample restrictions

These checks confirm that the age and calendar-year restrictions were applied as intended.

```{r verify-restrictions}
verification <- tibble(
  Check = c(
    "Number of observations",
    "Minimum age",
    "Maximum age",
    "Earliest calendar year",
    "Latest calendar year"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(analytic_dat),
    min(analytic_dat$edad_ano_creacion_caso),
    max(analytic_dat$edad_ano_creacion_caso),
    min(analytic_dat$year),
    max(analytic_dat$year)
  )
)

kable(verification)
```

## Records by calendar year

This table shows the number of observations in the preliminary analytic dataset for each calendar year.

```{r records-by-year}
analytic_dat %>%
  count(year, name = "n") %>%
  kable(
    col.names = c("Calendar year", "n")

```

# 4. Create Aim 1 analysis variables

This section creates clearly named analysis variables while preserving the original registry variables.

At this stage, categories are retained as they appear in the source data. Categories may be collapsed later after reviewing the distributions in the real registry data.

```{r analysis-variables}
analytic_dat <- analytic_dat %>%
  
  # Add region labels
  left_join(
    region_codes,
    by = c("cmd_cod_deis_regi_benef" = "Region Code")
  ) %>%
  
  # Add country-of-origin labels
  left_join(
    country_codes,
    by = c("cmd_cod_pais_origen" = "Country Code")
  ) %>%
  
  mutate(
    
    # -------------------------
    # Outcome
    # -------------------------
    age = edad_ano_creacion_caso,
    
    # -------------------------
    # Primary exposure
    # -------------------------
    calendar_year = year,
    
    # -------------------------
    # Individual characteristics
    # -------------------------
    sex = if_else(
      is.na(cmd_sexo_benef),
      "Missing",
      cmd_sexo_benef
    ),
    
    chilean_foreign = if_else(
      is.na(cmd_cond_chile_extranj),
      "Missing",
      cmd_cond_chile_extranj
    ),
    
    fonasa_tramo = if_else(
      is.na(cmd_carga_tramo_benef),
      "Missing",
      cmd_carga_tramo_benef
    ),
    
    country_origin = case_when(
      is.na(cmd_cod_pais_origen) ~ "Missing",
      is.na(`Country Name`) ~ paste0(
        "Unmapped code: ", cmd_cod_pais_origen
      ),
      TRUE ~ `Country Name`
    ),
    
    # -------------------------
    # Structural characteristic
    # -------------------------
    region = case_when(
      is.na(cmd_cod_deis_regi_benef) ~ "Missing",
      is.na(`Region name`) ~ paste0(
        "Unmapped code: ", cmd_cod_deis_regi_benef
      ),
      TRUE ~ `Region name`
    ),
    
    # -------------------------
    # Clinical setting variables
    # Retained for descriptive purposes
    # -------------------------
    establishment_level = if_else(
      is.na(desc_nivel_estab_crea_caso),
      "Missing",
      desc_nivel_estab_crea_caso
    ),
    
    establishment_type = if_else(
      is.na(desc_tipo_estab_crea_caso),
      "Missing",
      desc_tipo_estab_crea_caso
    ),
    
    # -------------------------
    # Case status variables
    # -------------------------
    ipd_confirmed = if_else(
      is.na(ipd_cofirmado),
      "Missing",
      ipd_cofirmado
    ),
    
    ipd_discarded = if_else(
      is.na(ipd_descartado),
      "Missing",
      ipd_descartado
    )
  )
```

# 5. Descriptive characteristics of preliminary analytic sample

For now, this section provides a broad descriptive summary of the preliminary analytic sample.

Categories are intentionally not collapsed at this stage.

## Overall sample size

```{r table1-n}
table1_n <- tibble(
  Characteristic = "Total analytic sample",
  Category = "",
  n = nrow(analytic_dat),
  Percent = NA_real_
)

kable(table1_n)
```

## Age

```{r table1-age}
age_table <- tibble(
  Characteristic = c(
    "Age",
    "Age",
    "Age",
    "Age",
    "Age"
  ),
  Category = c(
    "Mean (SD)",
    "Median",
    "Minimum",
    "Maximum",
    "Missing"
  ),
  Value = c(
    paste0(
      round(mean(analytic_dat$age, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      " (",
      round(sd(analytic_dat$age, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      ")"
    ),
    round(median(analytic_dat$age, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    min(analytic_dat$age, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(analytic_dat$age, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(is.na(analytic_dat$age))
  )
)

kable(age_table)
```

## Helper function for categorical characteristics

```{r table1-helper}
table1_cat <- function(data, variable, characteristic_name) {
  
  data %>%
    count({{ variable }}, name = "n") %>%
    mutate(
      Characteristic = characteristic_name,
      Category = as.character({{ variable }}),
      Percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)
    ) %>%
    select(
      Characteristic,
      Category,
      n,
      Percent
    )
}
```

# 6. Descriptive temporal trends

This section examines changes in age at diagnosis/case creation across calendar years.

## Age at diagnosis by calendar year

```{r age-by-year}
age_by_year <- analytic_dat %>%
  group_by(calendar_year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_age = sd(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_age = median(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(
  age_by_year,
  digits = 1,
  col.names = c(
    "Calendar year",
    "n",
    "Mean age",
    "SD",
    "Median age"
  )
)
```

## Overall mean age trend

```{r mean-age-trend}
ggplot(
  age_by_year,
  aes(
    x = calendar_year,
    y = mean_age
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2005, 2023, by = 2)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Age at Diagnosis by Calendar Year",
    x = "Calendar year",
    y = "Mean age at diagnosis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Median age trend

```{r median-age-trend}
ggplot(
  age_by_year,
  aes(
    x = calendar_year,
    y = median_age
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2005, 2023, by = 2)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Age at Diagnosis by Calendar Year",
    x = "Calendar year",
    y = "Median age at diagnosis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Mean age trend by sex

```{r age-trend-sex}
age_by_year_sex <- analytic_dat %>%
  group_by(
    calendar_year,
    sex
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  age_by_year_sex,
  aes(
    x = calendar_year,
    y = mean_age,
    group = sex,
    linetype = sex
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2005, 2023, by = 2)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Age at Diagnosis by Sex and Calendar Year",
    x = "Calendar year",
    y = "Mean age at diagnosis",
    linetype = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Mean age trend by Chilean/foreign status

```{r age-trend-migration}
age_by_year_migration <- analytic_dat %>%
  group_by(
    calendar_year,
    chilean_foreign
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  age_by_year_migration,
  aes(
    x = calendar_year,
    y = mean_age,
    group = chilean_foreign,
    linetype = chilean_foreign
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2005, 2023, by = 2)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Age at Diagnosis by Chilean/Foreign Status and Calendar Year",
    x = "Calendar year",
    y = "Mean age at diagnosis",
    linetype = "Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
